design_detail: Critical narrative review written in response to Hart et al. (2012), re-examining the same literature plus imaging and preclinical evidence.
can_establish: Whether Hart et al.'s reading of the primary studies holds; which lines of evidence support cognitive decline in at least a subset of users.
cannot_establish: Causation in humans; the authors acknowledge the absence of prospective pre-use data.

sample.selection_effects: Same vulnerability as any narrative review; written as a rebuttal.

comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Acknowledged; the authors argue that converging imaging and animal evidence makes a causal contribution plausible.

outcomes.operationalization: Argues that small group-level effects can be clinically meaningful at the tail of the distribution and for daily functioning.

interpretation_gap.results_show: A reasoned case that deficits exist in a subset of heavy users and that the evidence is stronger than Hart et al. allow.
interpretation_gap.claimed: Title asks whether methamphetamine 'causes cognitive decline'; the evidence reviewed is largely cross-sectional, so the causal question remains open by the authors' own account.

replication.where_it_stands: The exchange defines the two readings presented in the debate box.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: Narrative rebuttal; same treatment as Hart et al. (2012): used for its arguments, not as a quantitative synthesis.
